gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, at maker-store prices today, the 1 kWh class that covers a humidifier-off week via DC starts at $399 (ALLPOWERS P1800, 1,024 Wh), or that BLUETTI sells the 1,024 Wh Elite 100 V2 for the same $499 as the AC180 ChatGPT carded, at 25 lb against the AC180's 35.27 lb.
standout_why: I compared four pages. willitrunpower.com (cited) prices only AC180 $499, Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 $559, RIVER 2 Pro $389 sale, RIVER 3 Plus $299, Explorer 2000 v2 $899 sale and DELTA 2 Max $1,049, and shows 'See maker' for its own top pick DELTA 3 Plus and for Anker C1000. juicebench.com prices only Explorer 300 v2, Explorer 1000 v2 and AC180. amphourly.com gives no prices. preparedstates.com (cited) names no models. None of them lists the Elite 100 V2, P1800, DELTA 3 Classic, DELTA 3 Max or Anker S2000, or prices any of them. ChatGPT's own cards were AC180 '$449–$499', C1000 Gen 2 $549.99, C2000X Gen 2 $999.99 and DELTA 2 Max $1,049. I could not open the cited Reddit C300 thread (fetch blocked).
decides: For a dry week (humidifier and heated tube off, DC, about 100 Wh a night per our page), any LFP unit of about 1 kWh covers 7 nights, so price and weight decide the pick. The Elite 100 V2 matches the AC180's $499 at about 10 lb less. The P1800 at $399 is the cheapest. RIVER 2 Pro (768 Wh) falls short at about 6.5 nights. For a humid week via AC (450 Wh a night per our page), 7 nights need about 3.7 kWh nameplate at 85% usable, so no unit priced at $1,199 or less covers it. The Elite 300 (3,014 Wh, $1,199) gives about 5.7 nights. The cheapest 2 kWh units today are the Anker SOLIX S2000 ($699.99 on Amazon, 2,010 Wh) and the DELTA 3 Max Series ($879, 2,048 Wh), both below Elite 200 V2 ($899), Explorer 2000 v2 ($999) and DELTA 2 Max ($1,049). That confirms the 1 kWh pick only for heating-off. The AC180 should give way to a lighter or cheaper 1 kWh unit as the lead pick.
